main_text.p: Hazaeli vt moueret castra, & à ciuitatis obsidione desisteret. Quare, permisit Deus; vt eius satellites {1}Iozachar & Iozabad aduersus eum coniurarent, & vsq; ad internecionem percuterent; sed percusso-res ipsos, non ita multò post, Amazias Ioæ filius, & in regno successor, gladio percussit: {m}filios autem eorum, non occi-dit (inquit Scriptura) quasi dixisset, vel consuetudinem fuisse, vt in causa perduellionis, etiam filij vnà cum patribus poenas luerent; vel certè mereri patres, vt etiam luerent filij, licèt ipsi filij non mererentur, iuxta illud: {n}Non morien-tur patres pro filijs, neq; filij pro patribus,4.Reg.12.Cap.14.Deut.24. Ezec.18. sed vnufquifq;[?] in peccato suo morietur. Fi-lijs igitur pepercit quidem Amazias, patribus non item, vtcunque parentis sui interitu,sibi ad regni gubernacula a-ditum patefecissent. Non enim bonis Principibus
Nam, vel exempli causa, {p}Regi tuenda maxime Regum est salus.
Veruntamen, Amazias quoque à suis subditis interfectus, & in eius solium suffectusLucan.Seneca.

page.notes: The italic opening line is running text, not a heading. The word "Quare," is underlined in the scan, which is not marked here. The first margin note carries the mark "1" and reads "14.Reg.12." in the scan; the leading 1 may be the mark, so the note is read as 4.Reg.12. The page number may be the Roman-style numeral I rather than 1. The superscript marks in the text (1, m, n) are shown in braces as printed. The marginal notes are short and are copied as "Lucan." and "Seneca." with their marks o and p. The first line of this part is a fragment of the sentence continuing from the upper part of the page. The word "vnufquifq;" in the first line is uncertain, and so is the spelling "patefecissent", which the scan shows as a long-s-like form. The reference marks o and p are small and were read from the scan.
